material_implications.statement: Magma pushing up from the mantle creates new crust at spreading centers.

evidence.quote: Divergent boundaries occur along spreading centers where plates are moving apart and new crust is created by magma pushing up from the mantle.

support.statement: Magma pushing up from the mantle creates new crust at spreading centers.

material_implications.statement: Seafloor spreading over millions of years has resulted in plate movement of thousands of kilometers.

evidence.quote: This rate may seem slow by human standards, but because this process has been going on for millions of years, it has resulted in plate movement of thousands of kilometers.

support.statement: Seafloor spreading over millions of years has resulted in plate movement of thousands of kilometers.

material_implications.statement: Seafloor spreading caused the Atlantic Ocean to grow from a small inlet into its present vast ocean.

evidence.quote: Seafloor spreading over the past 100 to 200 million years has caused the Atlantic Ocean to grow from a tiny inlet of water between the continents of Europe, Africa, and the Americas into the vast ocean that exists today.

support.statement: Seafloor spreading caused the Atlantic Ocean to grow from a small inlet into its present vast ocean.

material_implications.statement: The consequences of plate movement include widening existing ground cracks and the appearance of new ones around Krafla Volcano.

evidence.quote: Here, existing ground cracks have widened and new ones appear every few months.

support.statement: The consequences of plate movement include widening existing ground cracks and the appearance of new ones around Krafla Volcano.

material_implications.statement: The displacements at Krafla were caused by rifting.

evidence.quote: Between 1975 and 1984, the displacements caused by rifting totalled about 7 m.

support.statement: The displacements at Krafla were caused by rifting.

material_implications.statement: Ground rise and abrupt dropping signalled an impending eruption.

evidence.quote: the ground would gradually rise 1-2 m before abruptly dropping, signalling an impending eruption.

support.statement: Ground rise and abrupt dropping signalled an impending eruption.

material_implications.statement: Spreading processes tore Saudi Arabia away from the rest of Africa, forming the Red Sea.

evidence.quote: In East Africa, spreading processes have already torn Saudi Arabia away from the rest of the African continent, forming the Red Sea.

support.statement: Spreading processes tore Saudi Arabia away from the rest of Africa, forming the Red Sea.

material_implications.statement: When continental crust stretches beyond its limits, tension cracks appear on Earth's surface.

evidence.quote: When the continental crust stretches beyond its limits, tension cracks begin to appear on the Earth's surface.

support.statement: When continental crust stretches beyond its limits, tension cracks appear on Earth's surface.

material_implications.statement: Rising magma puts more pressure on the crust.

evidence.quote: The rising magma, whether or not it erupts, puts more pressure on the crust to produce additional fractures and, ultimately, the rift zone.

support.statement: Rising magma puts more pressure on the crust.

material_implications.statement: Magma pressure produces additional fractures in the crust.

evidence.quote: The rising magma, whether or not it erupts, puts more pressure on the crust to produce additional fractures and, ultimately, the rift zone.

support.statement: Magma pressure produces additional fractures in the crust.

material_implications.statement: Crustal fractures contribute ultimately to the formation of a rift zone.

evidence.quote: The rising magma, whether or not it erupts, puts more pressure on the crust to produce additional fractures and, ultimately, the rift zone.

support.statement: Crustal fractures contribute ultimately to the formation of a rift zone.

material_implications.statement: Jet streams form when warm and cold air masses meet in the atmosphere.

evidence.quote: Jet streams form when warm air masses meet cold air masses in the atmosphere.

support.statement: Jet streams form when warm and cold air masses meet in the atmosphere.

material_implications.statement: When warmer air masses meet cooler air masses, the warmer air rises.

evidence.quote: the warmer air rises up higher in the atmosphere while cooler air sinks down to replace the warm air.

support.statement: When warmer air masses meet cooler air masses, the warmer air rises.

material_implications.statement: When warmer air masses meet cooler air masses, the cooler air sinks to replace the warm air.

evidence.quote: the warmer air rises up higher in the atmosphere while cooler air sinks down to replace the warm air.

support.statement: When warmer air masses meet cooler air masses, the cooler air sinks to replace the warm air.

material_implications.statement: The upward movement of warmer air contributes to the creation of an air current.

evidence.quote: the warmer air rises up higher in the atmosphere while cooler air sinks down to replace the warm air. This movement creates an air current, or wind.

support.statement: The upward movement of warmer air contributes to the creation of an air current.

material_implications.statement: The downward movement of cooler air contributes to the creation of an air current.

evidence.quote: the warmer air rises up higher in the atmosphere while cooler air sinks down to replace the warm air. This movement creates an air current, or wind.

support.statement: The downward movement of cooler air contributes to the creation of an air current.

material_implications.statement: The movement of warm and cool air creates an air current, or wind.

evidence.quote: This movement creates an air current, or wind.

support.statement: The movement of warm and cool air creates an air current, or wind.

material_implications.statement: Jet-stream formation produces a jet stream.

evidence.quote: Jet streams form when warm air masses meet cold air masses in the atmosphere.

support.statement: Jet-stream formation produces a jet stream.

material_implications.statement: Uneven solar heating produces warmer equatorial areas and colder polar areas, creating a temperature difference.

evidence.quote: The Sun doesn’t heat the whole Earth evenly. That’s why areas near the equator are hot and areas near the poles are cold.

support.statement: Uneven solar heating produces warmer equatorial areas and colder polar areas, creating a temperature difference.

material_implications.statement: Dramatic temperature differences between warm and cool air masses can increase jet-stream speed.

evidence.quote: dramatic temperature differences between the warm and cool air masses can cause jet streams to move at much higher speeds

support.statement: Dramatic temperature differences between warm and cool air masses can increase jet-stream speed.

material_implications.statement: A powerful jet stream can give an airplane a boost when it travels in the same direction.

evidence.quote: if an airplane flies in a powerful jet stream and they are traveling in the same direction, the airplane can get a boost.

support.statement: A powerful jet stream can give an airplane a boost when it travels in the same direction.

material_implications.statement: Fast-moving air currents in a jet stream transport weather systems across the United States.

evidence.quote: The fast-moving air currents in a jet stream can transport weather systems across the United States

support.statement: Fast-moving air currents in a jet stream transport weather systems across the United States.

material_implications.statement: Jet streams affect temperature as they transport weather systems.

evidence.quote: transport weather systems across the United States, affecting temperature and precipitation.

support.statement: Jet streams affect temperature as they transport weather systems.

material_implications.statement: Jet streams affect precipitation as they transport weather systems.

evidence.quote: transport weather systems across the United States, affecting temperature and precipitation.

support.statement: Jet streams affect precipitation as they transport weather systems.

material_implications.statement: Jet streams typically move storms from west to east.

evidence.quote: Jet streams typically move storms and other weather systems from west to east.

support.statement: Jet streams typically move storms from west to east.

material_implications.statement: Storms tend to follow the edge of the jet stream.

evidence.quote: Storms tend to follow the edge of the jet stream

support.statement: Storms tend to follow the edge of the jet stream.

material_implications.statement: The difference between cool and warm air creates turbulent conditions for storms.

evidence.quote: where the difference between cool and warm air creates the turbulent conditions for storms.

support.statement: The difference between cool and warm air creates turbulent conditions for storms.

material_implications.statement: A weather system that remains in one place can cause a heat wave.

evidence.quote: if a weather system is far away from a jet stream, it might stay in one place, causing heat waves or floods.

support.statement: A weather system that remains in one place can cause a heat wave.

material_implications.statement: A weather system that remains in one place can cause a flood.

evidence.quote: if a weather system is far away from a jet stream, it might stay in one place, causing heat waves or floods.

support.statement: A weather system that remains in one place can cause a flood.

material_implications.statement: Introduction of a bill precedes its referral to a committee.

evidence.quote: Once a Member of the House or Senate introduces a bill, it is typically referred to the committee (or committees) in that chamber with jurisdiction over its elements.

support.statement: Introduction of a bill precedes its referral to a committee.

material_implications.statement: A markup precedes the committee's majority vote to report a bill.

evidence.quote: The markup concludes when the committee agrees, by majority vote, to report the bill (with any recommended changes adopted in the markup) to its chamber.

support.statement: A markup precedes the committee's majority vote to report a bill.

material_implications.statement: The committee's majority vote causes the committee to report the bill.

evidence.quote: The markup concludes when the committee agrees, by majority vote, to report the bill (with any recommended changes adopted in the markup) to its chamber.

support.statement: The committee's majority vote causes the committee to report the bill.

material_implications.statement: A motion to proceed precedes the Senate's agreement to that motion.

evidence.quote: bills are brought to the floor only after the Senate agrees to a motion (typically offered by the majority leader) to proceed to a specific bill

support.statement: A motion to proceed precedes the Senate's agreement to that motion.

material_implications.statement: Stars form from nebulae.

evidence.quote: There are nebulae all around our galaxy, and it’s from these nebulae that stars and planets form.

support.statement: Stars form from nebulae.

material_implications.statement: Planets form from nebulae.

evidence.quote: There are nebulae all around our galaxy, and it’s from these nebulae that stars and planets form.

support.statement: Planets form from nebulae.

material_implications.statement: Material sticking together forms a large mass.

evidence.quote: When enough material is available, it begins to stick together forming a large mass.

support.statement: Material sticking together forms a large mass.

material_implications.statement: A mass can grow large enough to form a planet.

evidence.quote: In time, the mass can grow large enough to form a planet or even a new star.

support.statement: A mass can grow large enough to form a planet.

material_implications.statement: A mass can grow large enough to form a new star.

evidence.quote: In time, the mass can grow large enough to form a planet or even a new star.

support.statement: A mass can grow large enough to form a new star.

material_implications.statement: A supernova has enough energy to make gas and dust in nearby nebulae start swirling.

evidence.quote: Some big stars can explode, something called a supernova, and that explosion has enough energy to make the gas and dust in nearby nebulae start swirling and spinning about.

support.statement: A supernova has enough energy to make gas and dust in nearby nebulae start swirling.

material_implications.statement: A supernova has enough energy to make gas and dust in nearby nebulae start spinning.

evidence.quote: Some big stars can explode, something called a supernova, and that explosion has enough energy to make the gas and dust in nearby nebulae start swirling and spinning about.

support.statement: A supernova has enough energy to make gas and dust in nearby nebulae start spinning.

material_implications.statement: The swirling caused material in the nebula to fall into its center.

evidence.quote: As this happened, it caused a lot of the material in the nebula to fall into its center, and that’s where the Sun started forming.

support.statement: The swirling caused material in the nebula to fall into its center.

material_implications.statement: The spinning caused material in the nebula to fall into its center.

evidence.quote: As this happened, it caused a lot of the material in the nebula to fall into its center, and that’s where the Sun started forming.

support.statement: The spinning caused material in the nebula to fall into its center.

material_implications.statement: Collisions among gas and dust formed little pieces of metal and rock.

evidence.quote: Meanwhile, the rest of the gas and dust in the nebula began colliding and sticking together, making little pieces of metal and rock.

support.statement: Collisions among gas and dust formed little pieces of metal and rock.

material_implications.statement: Many collisions over a long time formed the eight planets.

evidence.quote: These were young planets, and eventually, over a long time and through many, many collisions, our eight planets were formed – Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

support.statement: Many collisions over a long time formed the eight planets.

material_implications.statement: Planet formation produced the eight planets.

evidence.quote: These were young planets, and eventually, over a long time and through many, many collisions, our eight planets were formed – Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

support.statement: Planet formation produced the eight planets.
